pairs.subject: templates-scaffolding
pairs.evidence: app/features/shared/renderTemplate.ts:161 The JD template catalog has one pure, deterministic mapping from (template body, data, output-language tokens) to a rendered JD. The client preview and the server build both call it, so the preview shows what Generate produces. Every write door also checks bodies against one closed token vocabulary.

techniques.evidence: app/features/shared/renderTemplate.ts:1 The mapping is one pure function shared by the live preview and the server render, so the preview recomputes the real result instead of being a stock screenshot. The provenance stamp (the JD's build intent records templateId) lives outside this context.

app/features/shared/renderTemplate.ts:361 Admission bar at one door: both the create and update validators run the unknown-token, length and empty checks, and the API and the manager share them. The seeded default is held to the same bar by a test (renderTemplate.test.ts 'the default template body has no unknown placeholders'). Retirement and dedupe live in the store/UI, not here.

app/features/shared/renderTemplate.ts:96 The seeded default no longer bakes in the author's English headings. Its structural scaffolding and fallbacks are tokens resolved from the adopter's output language at render time.

app/features/shared/renderTemplate.ts:158 A JD template needs no credentials, services or sibling entities. Its only prerequisite, the localized token map, is a required parameter that the type system enforces.

app/features/shared/renderTemplate.ts:93 The seeded payload is a code constant and user templates are authored in the app, so no catalog payload crosses a trust domain and there is no manifest or digest to bind.

app/features/shared/renderTemplate.ts:400 No 'template improved since you adopted' offer exists. A rendered JD is plain divorced markdown and the client template shape carries no version to compare against.
